newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK COURT RULES PRESIDENTIAL REFERENDUM LEGAL.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK COURT RULES PRESIDENTIAL REFERENDUM LEGAL.

text.p: Slovakia's Constitutional Court on Wendesday rejected a motion by deputies of the governing coalition to declare a referendum on direct presidential elections illegal.

"The question of whether or not the constitution can be changed by referendum is valid and a change in the constitution can be the subject of a referendum," spokewoman Mariana Mochnacova told Reuters from the court's seat in Kosice, eastern Slovakia.

The ruling removes the final obstacle in the path ahead of this weekend's referendum on whether the president should be elected directly instead of by a weighted majority in parliament as is currently the case.

The court, however, said the text of a new version of the constitution concerning direct presidential elections, appended to the referendum question by President Michal Kovac, was irrelevant and contrary to the constitution.

"Insofar as the citizens' vote in favour of changing the constitution to direct presidential elections is concerned, this is valid, but the further form in which this will be done remains open," Mochnacova said.
